newsitem.title: UK: Dollar claws back ground vs mark, steadies vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar claws back ground vs mark, steadies vs yen.

text.p: The dollar clawed back above 1.71 marks, but struggled to extend its rebound amid lingering concern European economic and monetary union may be delayed.
Talk EMU may not start in 1999 resurfaced after France asked on Monday for time to consider a pact which requires countries to maintain fiscal discipline after they join EMU.

Short-covering and assurances from European Union officials that the French request won't delay the launch of the European single currency lifted the dollar from the one-week low it set against the mark Monday. Still, traders expected it to hold below 1.72 marks until France reveals its stance on the pact.

"A great deal was made of the French announcement in London, but there is a somewhat different attitude towards it in Europe," said Keith Lewis, the manager of treasury markets at American Express Bank.
"While worries about EMU persist, (dollar/mark) will remain in a 1.69 to 1.72 range, but so much still favours the dollar that this is being viewed as a trading opportunity."
The dollar was steady against the yen, meantime, before the release of Japanese current account data later on Tuesday.
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7139/49 at 1035 GMT from its 1.7020 low Monday and 1.7055/60 late yesterday in Europe.
Dollar/yen was at 112.60/70 from 112.65/75 Monday. Mark/yen drifted down to 65.70/72 from 66.05/08 late Monday but held above the 21-month low around 65.20 it had set yesterday.
French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said Tuesday Paris needs more than a week to study the budget deficit stability pact and carry out an audit of state finances.

European Union officials have tried to calm market nerves by saying the move was not a precursor to renegotiating the pact. Also, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Tuesday there had been no change in the French government's "basic position," and predicted that the euro would be launched on time.

"Things have calmed down a bit after the French announcement yesterday, and it's likely we'll see some sort of deal on the stability pact," said Nick Stamencovic, an economist at DKB International. "But until then the mark should remain supported."
Meantime, the dollar also stabilised against the yen amid Japanese calls for a reduction in wild swings in currencies.

Speaking a day after the dollar tumbled more than two yen to a six-month low of 111.80, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said currency moves have been excessive and that Japan will combat such swings in an appropriate and timely way.
He also said Japan will discuss exchange rates and its trade surplus with other members of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations at their June 20-22 meeting in Denver.

Expectations America also doesn't want too steep a decline in the dollar/yen exchange rate also supported the dollar. U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and his deputy, Lawrence Summers, said Monday the U.S. still favours a strong dollar.

Traders are now looking to take their cue from Japanese current account data published later Tuesday, with economists polled by Reuters expecting the surplus to rise to 1.1 trillion yen from 1.0 trillion yen in March.
"The focus for dollar/yen is the figures that are coming out overnight, and no-one is going to be an agressive buyer before then," said Lewis at American Express Bank.
